questions.stem_en: An Amazon ECS service runs on EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. Service Auto Scaling with target tracking adds tasks during traffic peaks, but many new tasks stay in the PENDING state because the instances have no free capacity. The company wants the number of instances to grow and shrink automatically with the tasks' resource needs, without paying for idle peak capacity all day and without writing custom code. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices_en.text: Create an Auto Scaling group capacity provider with managed scaling and a targetCapacity, and use it for the service.
Raise the Auto Scaling group's minimum size to the number of instances needed at the daily peak.
Schedule an AWS Lambda function that counts PENDING tasks every minute and changes the Auto Scaling group's desired capacity.
Change the service's target tracking policy to a lower CPU target so that tasks are added earlier during traffic peaks.

explanation.summary: Auto Scaling グループのキャパシティープロバイダーでマネージドスケーリングを有効にし、targetCapacity を設定すると、タスクが使うリソースに合わせて ECS がインスタンスのスケールアウトとスケールインを管理します。インスタンスの数がタスクの必要に追いつき、独自のコードも要りません。

per_choice.A: 正しい。ECS がタスクのリソースの使用に基づいてインスタンスを増減するので、PENDING のタスクが解消し、使われない容量も減らせます。
per_choice.B: PENDING は減りますが、山の分のインスタンスを一日中動かすことになり、費用の要件に反します。
per_choice.C: 動きますが、インスタンスの数を調整する独自のコードを作って保守する必要があります。
per_choice.D: タスクが早く増えるだけで、インスタンスの容量は増えないため、PENDING のタスクは解消しません。

references.quote: You turn on managed scaling when you create the Amazon ECS Auto Scaling group capacity provider.
Amazon ECS then manages the scale-in and scale-out actions based on the resource utilization that your tasks use.
Automatic scaling is the ability to increase or decrease the desired number of tasks in your Amazon ECS service automatically.

questions.stem_en: A company runs an interruption-tolerant queue worker as an Amazon ECS service on AWS Fargate. To reduce cost, the company wants most tasks to run on Fargate Spot. The service must keep processing even when Fargate Spot capacity is unavailable, and each task must finish its cleanup work before it stops when Spot capacity is reclaimed. Which actions should a DevOps engineer take to meet these requirements? (Choose TWO.)

choices_en.text: Use a capacity provider strategy that includes both the FARGATE and FARGATE_SPOT capacity providers, with most tasks placed on FARGATE_SPOT.
Use only the FARGATE_SPOT capacity provider, and rely on Fargate to replace Spot capacity with on-demand capacity when Spot is unavailable.
Handle the SIGTERM signal in the container to run the cleanup work, and keep the cleanup within the task's stopTimeout.
Use one capacity provider strategy that combines FARGATE_SPOT with an Auto Scaling group capacity provider for on-demand EC2 instances.
Run the service with a single task on FARGATE_SPOT so that only one task is affected by each interruption.

explanation.summary: Fargate は Spot の容量をオンデマンドの容量に置き換えないため、Spot が使えない時も処理を続けるには、戦略に FARGATE も入れておく必要があります。Spot の容量が回収される時は 2 分前に警告があり、コンテナの中で SIGTERM を受けて後片付けを行います（stopTimeout の既定は 30 秒）。

per_choice.A: 正しい。ほとんどを Spot に置いて費用を下げつつ、FARGATE のタスクで Spot が使えない時も処理を続けられます。
per_choice.B: Fargate は Spot の容量をオンデマンドに置き換えないため、Spot が使えない間はタスクが起動できず処理が止まるおそれがあります。
per_choice.C: 正しい。後片付けをするには、コンテナの中で SIGTERM を受ける必要があります。
per_choice.D: 1 つのキャパシティープロバイダー戦略には、Fargate と Auto Scaling グループのキャパシティープロバイダーを一緒に入れられません。
per_choice.E: タスクが 1 つだけのサービスは、容量が戻るまで中断されたままになり、処理を続ける要件に反します。

references.quote: Fargate doesn't replace Spot capacity with on-demand capacity.
The SIGTERM signal must be received from within the container to perform any cleanup actions.
However, a capacity provider strategy can only contain either Fargate or Auto Scaling group capacity providers, but not both.
A service with only one task is interrupted until capacity is available.

questions.stem_en: A company deploys an Amazon ECS service with the rolling update (ECS) deployment controller. Last week, a new image that crashed at startup was deployed, and ECS kept trying to start new tasks until an engineer noticed and manually redeployed the previous task definition. The company wants failed deployments to be detected and returned to the last working deployment automatically, without changing the deployment controller. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices_en.text: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule for stopped tasks that invokes an AWS Lambda function to update the service with the previous task definition.
Switch the service to the AWS CodeDeploy blue/green deployment controller and configure automatic rollback in the deployment group.
Turn on the deployment circuit breaker for the service with the rollback option enabled.
Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm on the number of running tasks that notifies the engineers so they can redeploy the previous task definition.

explanation.summary: デプロイのサーキットブレーカーは、ローリング更新でタスクが安定した状態に達するかを判断する仕組みで、失敗したデプロイを COMPLETED の状態のデプロイへ自動でロールバックするオプションがあります。ローリング更新（ECS）のデプロイコントローラーのサービスでだけ使えるので、コントローラーを変えずに済みます。

per_choice.A: 動きますが、失敗の判断と戻しを Lambda 関数で作って保守する必要があり、組み込みの仕組みより手間がかかります。
per_choice.B: 自動で戻せますが、デプロイコントローラーを変えないという要件に反します。
per_choice.C: 正しい。今のローリング更新のまま、失敗を検知して最後に完了したデプロイへ自動で戻します。
per_choice.D: 通知だけで戻しは手作業のままで、自動で戻すという要件に合いません。

references.quote: The deployment circuit breaker has an option that will automatically roll back a failed deployment to the deployment that is in the COMPLETED state.
The deployment circuit breaker is only supported for Amazon ECS services that use the rolling update (ECS) deployment controller.
The deployment circuit breaker is the rolling update mechanism that determines if the tasks reach a steady state.
